subject: Transportation Systems
title: Lessons from the Titanic
description: A quick, practical guide to Lessons from the Titanic.

hook.text: In 1912, the 'unsinkable' Titanic struck an iceberg. Over 1,500 people died in freezing water.

buildup.text: There weren't enough lifeboats. Regulations allowed capacity for half the passengers on board.

discovery.text: The disaster led to SOLAS—the International Convention for Safety of Life at Sea, still in force today.

twist.text: SOLAS required lifeboats for all, 24-hour radio watch, and the creation of the International Ice Patrol.

climax.text: Every major maritime safety rule traces back to a disaster. Titanic was the catalyst for all of them.

punchline.text: The Titanic sank once. Its lessons saved millions.

quiz.question: What did the Titanic disaster lead to?
options: The SOLAS convention for maritime safety
